newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to scrap gas and electricity subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to scrap gas and electricity subsidies.

text.p: Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said on Thursday that Ukraine would raise natural gas and electricity prices in the second half of the year, cancelling a 20 percent government subsidy to residents.
"In the second half of 1997 we are planning to raise payment of tariffs to 100 percent," Lazarenko told Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi during a meeting attended by journalists.
Residents now pay 80 percent of the price of natural gas and electricity while industrial consumers pay the full price.

Lazarenko said in December that prices would stay flat in 1997, going against the wishes of the International Monetary Fund with which Ukraine is negotiating a $2.5-$3.0 billion Extended Fund Facility loan.
Lazarenko also forecast annual inflation for the year at 24.8 percent from 39.7 percent in 1996. "Now we have achieved a certain stabilisation on the monetary level," he said.
Lazarenko put the cost of state subsidies to gas consumers alone at $1.12 billion last year.
The energy ministry put the size of consumer debt to the sector at 3.9 billion hryvnias at the start of January, up from 2.1 billion hryvnias a year earlier.
